title: Agent Architecture
learning_outcomes: Explain language models as decision components and how it connects to agent architecture.
Apply the observe-act-result cycle in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for agent architecture and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers agent architecture through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Treat agentic systems as bounded loops over plans, state, tools, observations, and stopping conditions. Prefer deterministic workflows when they meet the need more reliably.
content.why_it_matters: Language models as decision components is part of the representation and generation mechanism. Follow the information flow from input representation to model computation to output selection, then distinguish the architecture's capabilities from limits caused by data, context, decoding choices, or compute.

items.title: The observe-act-result cycle
items.text: Use the observe-act-result cycle as a lens for understanding agent architecture. Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

items.title: Planning and task decomposition
items.text: Planning and task decomposition describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice language models as decision components within agent architecture: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
